intro: Hello and welcome to Vijay News English. It is Saturday, the twenty-eighth of November. Here are the top stories from India and around the world, with business, sports, cinema and technology.
outro: Those were the top stories right now. We will be back shortly with the latest updates. Keep watching Vijay News English.

stories.headline: PM Modi meets foreign ministers of 23 Indian Ocean nations
stories.headline_spoken: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met foreign ministers from twenty-three Indian Ocean nations in New Delhi.
facts: India hosted the 25th IORA Council of Ministers in Delhi
Ministers of Sri Lanka, Maldives and Mauritius attended
India chairs the Indian Ocean Rim Association till 2027
stories.body: India played host to the Indian Ocean this week. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met foreign ministers and heads of delegation from all twenty-three member states of the Indian Ocean Rim Association in New Delhi on Friday, the Prime Minister's Office said in a post on X. They were in the capital for the grouping's twenty-fifth Council of Ministers, chaired by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. India holds the chair until 2027, and the focus is on trade, maritime security and the blue economy.

stories.headline: India and US close to a trade deal, says Piyush Goyal
stories.headline_spoken: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says the India-US trade deal is close to the finish line.
facts: Goyal says the US trade deal is close to culmination
Talks aim to avoid higher US tariffs on Indian goods
Comments came after remarks by the US trade chief
stories.body: A long-awaited trade deal between India and the United States may finally be near. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told an industry conference on Friday that the deal is close to culmination, and that the process which held it back is now taking shape, Reuters reported. Both sides want to avoid higher American tariffs on Indian exports. For exporters of textiles, engineering goods and medicines, a deal could bring much-needed certainty.

stories.headline: President Murmu begins a three-day visit to Mizoram
stories.headline_spoken: President Droupadi Murmu begins a three-day visit to Mizoram today.
facts: President Murmu is in Mizoram from November 28 to 30
She is chief guest at the Mizoram University convocation
More than 11 state departments are coordinating arrangements
stories.body: President Droupadi Murmu begins a three-day visit to Mizoram today. Her main engagement is the convocation of Mizoram University at Tanhril in Aizawl, where she is the chief guest. The state government says more than eleven departments are working together on security, traffic and protocol for the visit. For the students graduating this year, the ceremony brings the nation's highest office to their campus.

stories.headline: Two years of India's campaign against child marriage
stories.headline_spoken: India marked two years of its nationwide campaign to end child marriage.
stories.stat_label: years of Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat
facts: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign completes two years
A national event marked the milestone on November 27
The campaign targets a child-marriage-free India
stories.source: Source: Ministry of Women and Child Development (PIB)
stories.body: A campaign that touches millions of families completed two years this week. The Ministry of Women and Child Development held a national event on Friday to mark two years of Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat, the nationwide drive against child marriage. The campaign works with states, schools and village communities to keep girls in education and stop early marriages, which harm their health and their futures.

stories.headline: Attacks on tankers and Saudi oil sites push oil prices higher
stories.headline_spoken: Fresh attacks on oil tankers and Saudi energy sites have pushed oil prices higher.
facts: Brent crude posted its first weekly gain this month
Houthi militants hit Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery
Tankers were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz
stories.body: The oil market is nervous again. Brent crude settled near ninety-five dollars a barrel on Friday and posted its first weekly gain in November, after attacks on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi energy sites, Reuters reported. Houthi militants struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery on Thursday, Bloomberg said. For India, which imports most of its oil, higher crude prices can mean costlier fuel and pressure on the rupee.

stories.headline: Sensex falls nearly 1,000 points as oil prices climb
stories.headline_spoken: The Sensex fell nearly one thousand points as rising oil prices hit market mood.
facts: Sensex fell 989 points to close at 83,339
Nifty 50 lost 277 points to end at 25,607
IT, auto and bank shares led the selling
stories.body: It was a rough Friday on Dalal Street. The Sensex fell nine hundred and eighty-nine points, or about one point two percent, to close at eighty-three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine. The Nifty fifty slipped two hundred and seventy-seven points to twenty-five thousand six hundred and seven. Profit-taking in IT, auto and banking shares, higher crude oil prices and uncertainty over the India-US trade deal weighed on investors, while metal stocks held up.

stories.headline: India face China in the Women's Asian Champions Trophy final
stories.headline_spoken: India's women's hockey team faces China in the Asian Champions Trophy final tonight.
facts: India beat Malaysia 6-2 to reach the final
The final against China is at 7 PM in Bhopal
India chase a third straight title and fourth overall
stories.body: Indian women's hockey has a big night ahead. The defending champions take on China in the final of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal at seven this evening. India reached the final unbeaten, thrashing Malaysia six-two in the semi-final on Friday, with Deepika leading the scoring charts. A win would give India a third straight title and a record fourth crown, in front of a home crowd.

stories.headline: IFFI 2026 closes in Goa as the Golden Peacock is announced
stories.headline_spoken: The International Film Festival of India closes in Goa today with the Golden Peacock award.
facts: The 57th IFFI closes in Goa on November 28
The Golden Peacock carries a prize of 51 lakh rupees
Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers closes the festival
stories.source: Source: IFFI, Business Upturn, Argus News
stories.body: After nine days of world cinema, the fifty-seventh International Film Festival of India closes in Goa today. The festival, themed Stories Without Borders and directed by Ashutosh Gowariker, brought films from eighty-six countries. The closing ceremony will award the Golden Peacock for best film, which carries a prize of fifty-one lakh rupees. Singaporean director Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers is the closing film.

stories.headline: US approves SpaceX plan for one million AI satellites
stories.headline_spoken: The US regulator has conditionally approved SpaceX's plan for up to one million AI computing satellites.
facts: FCC gave SpaceX conditional approval on November 25
The Starmind satellites would run AI data centres
First satellite must be in orbit by November 2033
stories.body: Could the next data centres be in space? America's Federal Communications Commission has conditionally approved SpaceX's plan to launch up to one million satellites, called Starmind, that would run artificial intelligence workloads in orbit, TechCrunch reported. Supporters say solar-powered computing in space could ease AI's huge demand for energy. But the approval sets long deadlines, with the first satellite due by 2033, and astronomers have raised concerns.

stories.headline: New US computing rules slow Chinese AI models
stories.headline_spoken: New US computing rules are slowing the release of Chinese AI models.
facts: A US rule now needs licences for big overseas computing
Z.ai's GLM-5.5 model missed its November launch
The release may slip into 2027, Reuters reported
stories.source: Source: Reuters via AI Affairs, Distill Intelligence
stories.body: The global race in artificial intelligence just got harder for Chinese developers. A new US rule, in force since November nineteenth, requires licences for large overseas computing arrangements, roughly above the power of seven hundred and fifty advanced Nvidia chips. Chinese labs have been renting such capacity abroad. Reuters reported that Z dot ai's next major model, GLM five point five, missed its November launch and could slip into 2027.
